adapters.name: jules
adapters.note: ASYNC cloud agent: 'jules new' dispatches a session on the REMOTE repo, not this worktree (phase-1 limitation). 'jules remote list' alone says 'Must specify what to list' on exit 0, so the probe scopes it with --session.

probeRules.pattern: (?i)jules login|not signed in|sign in to jules

adapters.name: dsh
adapters.note: PILOT (#773). DeepSeek Harness (@deepseek-ai/dsh 0.2.0-rc.2, headless profile, --json event stream), run ONLY inside the agentic-board/dsh image built from containers/dsh - never on the host, so the command is docker and there is no npm install argv (the pin lives in containers/dsh/package.json + package-lock.json). The container gets the worktree as its only writable mount, a tmpfs /tmp (DSH_HOME, so dsh's session log dies with it), a read-only root, no host home, no docker socket, a non-root user, CPU/memory/pid limits and ONE host variable, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY - no GitHub token: dsh edits files, the host flow commits and opens the PR. The session-log upload (session-log-deepseek, on by default in 0.2.0-rc.2, carried inside the API request) and the OTLP telemetry are disabled by the image (no-upload.patch.yml + DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED), the image build fails if the composed config still mounts them, and --add-host points the telemetry collectors at 127.0.0.1. Headless dsh edits inside its workspace in its default workspace-write mode, so no bypass is needed (requiresBypass false, no bypassArgs). lowTrust: public repos only, docs/chore routes only, never a reviewer.

probeRules.note: --pull=never: a missing image is never fetched from a registry, it is reported.

probeRules.pattern: (?i)Cannot connect to the Docker daemon|error during connect|docker daemon is not running|dockerDesktopLinuxEngine

probeRules.reason: the sandbox entrypoint refused to start dsh (see its message)

probeRules.note: dsh prints 'dsh: <code>: <message>' on stderr and the same code in the --json turn_end event.
